header: Hindi and Bengali letter slips: plain code finds them, and I repair them only from the OTHER independent reading, never by invention. What the circular PRINTS is a record: a spelling slip in the printed circular ("ठेकेदारो", "त्यौहारिय") is kept exactly as printed, because a corrector, human or model, is wrong often enough (on the stored archive a strong model flagged 15 words and 4 of them were correct words). What is NOT a record is a slip of the READER: a letter of the wrong script (a Korean letter where "क्र" is printed), or a letter sequence that cannot occur in the language (a virama followed by a vowel sign). That kind can be detected without a dictionary, and the second reader (which read the same page independently) usually has the right word. So my steps are:
1. a token of the primary reading with such a defect is looked up in the checker's reading;
2. I replace it only with a clean token of the checker that fits (the stray letters stand for 1-4 letters of it) and that is the ONLY fit on the page, or stands next to the same neighbour word;
3. a defect with no such token is left as read and REPORTED, never guessed.

symbols.name: STRAY
doc: I leave Greek out on purpose: mu, omega and alpha are real symbols in a technical circular, while the other scripts never are

symbols.name: indicDefect
symbols.sig: export function indicDefect(token: string): IndicDefect | null
doc: Says what is wrong with one token (a word with its punctuation), or null. I only look at tokens that hold a Devanagari or Bengali letter or a stray letter.

symbols.name: canonicalIndic
doc: Gives the canonical form of the Hindi and Bengali words of a text (Unicode NFC, which writes ड़ ढ़ য় ড় ঢ় the one standard way), so a word typed in one form is found in the other. The letters are the same letters.

symbols.name: patternOf
doc: Builds the pattern a defective token stands for: I let each run of stray letters be 1 to 4 letters of the right word.

symbols.name: distance
symbols.sig: function distance(a: string, b: string, cap: number): number
doc: Levenshtein distance on code points, capped (returns cap + 1 when larger).

symbols.name: repairIndic
symbols.sig: export function repairIndic(primary: string, checker: string | null | undefined): { text: string; repairs: IndicRepair[]; unresolved: IndicUnresolved[] }
symbols.returns: { text: string; repairs: IndicRepair[]; unresolved: IndicUnresolved[] }
doc: Repairs the defective tokens of `primary` from `checker` (the other reading of the same page). Returns the repaired text, what was repaired, and what could not be. `checker` may be empty or null: then I repair nothing and report every defect.

behaviours: a Korean letter is a stray-script slip
a Cyrillic letter in a word is a slip
Greek mu / omega are real symbols, not a slip
a clean Hindi word is not a defect
a clean Bengali word is not a defect
a virama followed by a vowel sign is impossible
two vowel signs in a row are impossible
a word starting with a vowel sign is impossible
a Bengali virama + vowel sign is impossible
plain English and numbers are never a defect
a printed spelling slip is NOT a defect (kept as printed)
the Korean letter is replaced by the checker's word
with no second reading nothing is guessed, the slip is reported
a second reading without the word leaves the slip and reports it
only the defective token is touched: a printed slip is not 'corrected' even when the other reading differs
two possible words and no neighbour match: not guessed
two possible words, one stands next to the same neighbours: that one
a malformed sequence is replaced by the close clean word of the other reading
line breaks and spacing are kept
the precomposed Bengali ya-nukta (U+09DF) becomes the standard sequence
the precomposed Devanagari da-nukta (U+095C) becomes the standard sequence
a word typed either way is the same after canonicalIndic
English text is not changed
already canonical text is unchanged
a joiner typed inside a word does not split it
a query typed with the precomposed letter equals the stored form
English and quoted queries are unchanged
the upload text carries the repaired word
the summary mentions the correction
a slip the second reading cannot fix is reported in the log and the summary
a clean English page is unchanged and its summary has no letter-slip note
